chunks: “When it is the eve of Arafah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends two angels who examine the faces of the people. If they miss a man who had accustomed himself to hajj, one of them says to his companion: ‘O so-and-so, what happened to so-and-so?’ He said: then he says, ‘Allah knows best.’ He said: then one of them says, ‘O Allah, if poverty has prevented him from hajj, then enrich him; if debt has prevented him, then settle his debt for him; if illness has prevented him, then cure him; and if death has prevented him, then forgive him and have mercy on him.’”

key_terms.الْحَجَّ: hajj, the pilgrimage to the Sacred House
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: debt that hinders one from performing hajj
key_terms.عَشِيَّةُ عَرَفَةَ: the eve of Arafah, a sacred time connected to hajj
key_terms.فَاغْفِرْ لَهُ وَ ارْحَمْهُ: a supplication asking Allah for forgiveness and mercy for the deceased
key_terms.فَقْرٌ: poverty that prevents a person from traveling for hajj
key_terms.مَرَضٌ: illness that prevents participation in hajj
key_terms.مَوْتٌ: death as the cause of absence

ai.seo_question: What happens to a believer who regularly performed hajj but is absent on the eve of Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the virtue of those who regularly perform hajj and the special concern shown for them on the eve of Arafah. It conveys that if such a person is absent due to poverty, debt, illness, or death, supplication is made for his relief, forgiveness, and mercy.
